question: What did butter production in Bangladesh have to do with American share prices?
answer: Nothing, which was the point. David Leinweber searched a United Nations database for any series that tracked the S&P 500 and found Bangladeshi butter output explained 75% of its yearly moves over ten years. Adding US cheese and a sheep count pushed the fit to 99%. Outside those years, the model predicted nothing at all.
move: Search enough numbers and some will match anything by chance.
ask: When a pattern seems to predict something I care about, how many other patterns were tried and dropped?
reference: Leinweber, Stupid Data Miner Tricks: Overfitting the S&P 500, Journal of Investing, 2007
